title: Signal interoperability and epochal metrics playbook
content:
Overview:
This is a practical playbook for making signals (metrics + traces + contextual tags) interoperable across the stack and for introducing "epochal" metrics — lightweight, time-bucketed aggregates that bridge expensive raw telemetry and high-cardinality dashboards. Purpose is to reduce investigation time, bound trace cost, and provide dashboard widgets with stable contracts.

Why this vs existing docs:
- Many observability notes focus either on dashboards or on sampling rules. This doc stitches both concerns: how metric design and trace enrichment influence sampling budgets and dashboard UX.
- Introduces the term 'epochal metrics' to describe a compact aggregation layer we should standardize across teams.

Design principles (short):
- Contract-first widgets: widget owners define an input contract (keys + epoch window) that the ingestion/ETL must support.
- Minimal canonical trace envelope: capture only fields required for cross-layer joins and run deterministic sampling.
- Cost-aware sampling: per-tenant sampling budgets enforced at ingestion; fallbacks to epochal metrics when traces are cheap or saturated.
- Idempotent aggregation: epochal metrics should be re-aggregatable from raw events with stable keys and windows.

Canonical trace envelope (recommended minimal fields):
- trace_id (string)
- timestamp_iso (string)
- tenant_id (string)
- request_id (string)
- route (string) — API route or logical operation
- model_id (string) — canonical model alias used by routing
- kv_cache_warmth (enum: hot|warm|cold|unknown)
- latency_ms (number) — end-to-end token path latency
- sampling_reason (enum: probe|anomaly|always|manual|none)
- causation_tags (comma separated short tags)

Notes: keep the envelope compact so trace storage and transfer to debugging tools is bounded. Longer call graphs are stored only for sampled traces.

Epochal metrics: definition and rationale:
- Definition: a small set of pre-aggregated metrics emitted for short, fixed windows (epochs), e.g., 30s or 1m. Each epoch entry is keyed by the canonical join keys (tenant_id, route, model_id, epoch_start_iso).
- Example epochal metrics: total_requests, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, cache_miss_rate, tokens_emitted, traces_sampled_count.
- Rationale: dashboards can render near-real-time slices using epochal metrics even when full traces are unavailable or sampled down. Epochal metrics are cheap (rollups are small) and reduce the need for expensive cross-tenant queries on raw traces.

Epoch contract (recommended fields for each epoch record):
- epoch_start_iso
- epoch_window_secs
- tenant_id
- route
- model_id
- requests_total
- tokens_total
- latency_p50_ms
- latency_p95_ms
- cache_miss_fraction
- sampled_traces_count

How epochal metrics and sampling interact:
- Sampling budget exhausted -> increase epochal metric retention/window or fall back to synthetic probes for that tenant.
- When anomaly detector flags a metric delta in epochal stream (e.g., p95 jumps), trigger targeted sampling (sampling_reason=anomaly) for the next N epochs for affected keys.
- Use epochal sampled_traces_count to compute trace coverage. Dashboards should show "trace coverage" alongside latency panels.

Dashboard widget contract (example):
- Owner declares: required join keys (tenant+route+model), required epochs (30s/1m), and minimum trace_coverage threshold for enabling trace drill-down button.
- Widget ingestion returns either: epochal data (preferred) OR aggregated raw-metric fallback if epochs missing.
- Widgets must gracefully degrade (show coverage and a link to a small runbook) instead of silently hiding data.

Sampling policy (practical rules):
1) Baseline: sample 1 in 100 requests per tenant for normal traffic (configurable by SLA tier).
2) Probe sampling: independent 1 in 10 for synthetic probes and canary routes.
3) Anomaly-triggered sampling: when epochal metrics deviate beyond threshold, sample up to 1 in 5 for next 5 epochs for the affected keys.
4) Always-sample for security/compliance flagged tenants or audit routes.
5) Edge-case: for ultra-high-cardinality routes (>=10k distinct user keys per epoch), rely on epochal aggregates and targeted sampling anchored on route+model rather than user id.

Practical instrumentation checklist (short):
- [ ] Ensure SDK emits canonical envelope fields before any optional payload.
- [ ] Tag traces with model_id and route consistently across services (router, inference runtime, api-proxy).
- [ ] Emit epochal metrics at ingress or sampling proxy layer; keep aggregation idempotent.
- [ ] Configure sampling_policy per tenant in central config (link to ENG-1427).
- [ ] Add a dashboard tile for trace_coverage per tenant and route.

Investigation playbook (operator-facing):
1) Look at epochal p95 and trace_coverage for affected tenant+route. Is coverage < 0.01? If yes, we may be in a sampled-down state — start targeted sampling.
2) If coverage adequate, open sample traces: verify kv_cache_warmth and model_id consistency.
3) If cache_miss_fraction high and latency spike present, check prefix-warmth probe history and recent rollout tags.
4) Use request_id to locate full request logs (if linked) and cross-check with deployment rollout window.
5) If nothing obvious, increase sampling_reason=manual for next 3 epochs and tag suspected traces with investigation_id.

Runbook snippets (to copy/paste to pager message):
- "Latency spike observed on tenant=<tenant> route=<route> at <time>. p95 jumped from X->Y. Trace coverage: Z. Triggered targeted sampling for 5m. Assigned to oncall."

Developer guidance (small):
- Metric names should favor verbs for counters (requests_total) and nouns for gauges (kv_cache_warmth).
- Avoid embedding tenant or model ids in metric names; use tags for that.
- Keep high-cardinality tags out of default dashboard tiles; expose behind "zoom-in" flows.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- Epoch window sizing: 30s gives fast feedback but increases rows/churn. 1m is cheaper but slower. Need experiment across two busy tenants.
- How to represent multi-model fanout requests? Option A: emit epochal metrics per model_id (duplicates counts) vs Option B: include fanout_count in epoch row and keep model_id=primary. Which supports rollback analysis better?
- Backfills: epochal metrics must be reconstructable from raw logs for replay — enforce idempotent keys.

Implementation roadmap (next milestones):
- M1 (2 weeks): SDK envelope + central sampling policy flag implementation (PR: telemetry #231).
- M2 (4 weeks): Epochal aggregation job (30s/1m) and new dashboard tiles for trace_coverage and epochal p95.
- M3 (8 weeks): Targeted sampling automation (anomaly -> sampling escalation) + per-tenant budgets + runbook templates.

Quick links and references:
- ENG-1427 (sampling policy centralization)
- telemetry PR #231 (envelope and config knobs)
- Confluence page: Signal Interoperability Notes

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc short and operational — avoid rehashing tracing theory.
- Schedule 30 min sync with Miguel + Priya to pick epoch window default.
- Add a tiny demo dashboard that shows how widgets degrade when coverage low (good teaching tool).

Appendix: short example epoch row (CSV style)
epoch_start_iso,epoch_window_secs,tenant_id,route,model_id,requests_total,tokens_total,latency_p50_ms,latency_p95_ms,cache_miss_fraction,sampled_traces_count
2025-09-02T14:22:00Z,60,tenant-acme,/v1/generate,redwood-1.1,1234,98765,12,156,0.11,3

End.
